The Clock Above the Stairs

On the morning of the library's anniversary, the brass clock above the stairs stopped at 8:17, Theo carried a small ladder from the supply room and climbed toward it.[1] Guests would soon arrive, and the silent clock made the bright lobby feel strangely unfinished.

Theo first checked the battery, which still held a full charge.[2] He removed the clock's clear cover and watched the gears while gently turning the adjustment wheel. Most moved together, but one gear acted weird[3] near the top of each rotation.

A narrow strip of paper was caught between two teeth. It had torn from a maintenance label inside the case. In contrast,[4] Theo loosened the gear, lifted out the paper with tweezers, and returned the wheel to its position.

The second hand crossed 8:17 and continued around the dial. Theo stepped down as the first visitors entered. He had expected the repair to require a new part; instead, they[5] required patient observation and a scrap of paper no wider than a thread.

The Clock Above the Stairs

On the morning of the library's anniversary, the brass clock above the stairs stopped at 8:17; Theo carried a small ladder from the supply room and climbed toward it.[1] Guests would soon arrive, and the silent clock made the bright lobby feel strangely unfinished.

Theo first checked the battery, which still held a full charge.[2] He removed the clock's clear cover and watched the gears while gently turning the adjustment wheel. Most moved together, but one gear hesitated[3] near the top of each rotation.

A narrow strip of paper was caught between two teeth. It had torn from a maintenance label inside the case. Consequently,[4] Theo loosened the gear, lifted out the paper with tweezers, and returned the wheel to its position.

The second hand crossed 8:17 and continued around the dial. Theo stepped down as the first visitors entered. He had expected the repair to require a new part; instead, it[5] required patient observation and a scrap of paper no wider than a thread.
